clue.text: A craftsman can start to model in this, surprisingly

parts.note: a can is a tin

indicators.note: in places the first letter of model inside the word this before mixing
surprisingly signals the letters of this, with a letter put in, turning out in an unexpected order
start to points at the opening letter of model

explanation.surface: A metalworker could begin modelling in this material, unexpectedly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' looks like a verb but is the metal container. 'surprisingly' rearranges THMIS (M placed in the word this) into the second half.
explanation.definitionFit: A tinsmith is an artisan who makes and mends articles of tinplate.

clue.text: Popular song, the work of a craftsman

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a lay is a ballad or song

explanation.surface: A hit tune presented as a piece of fine handiwork.
explanation.definitionFit: Inlay is decorative work set into a surface by a skilled artisan.

clue.text: New comedies unknown to appear in this size of book

indicators.note: new suggests the letters are made over into a fresh order

parts.note: X is the mathematician's unknown quantity
taken as written

explanation.surface: Fresh comic plays to be published in a particular book format.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges COMEDIES plus X and TO. 'to appear in this' links fodder to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sextodecimo is a book format with sheets folded into sixteen leaves.

clue.text: Guileless girl out East set up hospital department

indicators.note: in a down clue set up means the girl's name, once trimmed, is written upwards
out means the compass letter is dropped from the name

parts.note: Connie is a girl's name
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department

explanation.surface: A naive young woman, with the East excluded, organised a ward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' drops the compass letter from the girl's name, leaving CONNI; in a down light 'set up' reads it upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone innocent is free of cunning or deceit, naive and artless.

clue.text: Be equipped for success? We may let an aggressive dog do it!

definitions.meaning: to have the qualities needed to succeed

definitions.text: We may let an aggressive dog do it!
definitions.meaning: read literally: a fierce dog that snatches something is allowed to keep what it grabs

explanation.surface: Advice on success turns into advice on handling a snappy dog.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the phrase literally: the dog keeps whatever it seizes.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes having the abilities required to succeed.

clue.text: Ring removed from highly ornate sailing-ship

indicators.note: removed says the ring-shaped letter is taken away from the ornate word

parts.note: baroque describes highly ornate style
O is shaped like a ring

explanation.surface: Decoration stripped from an over-elaborate vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A barque is a sailing vessel with three or more masts.

clue.text: A couple of lines in naughty poem

indicators.note: in places the article and the pair of lines inside the word for naughty

parts.note: bad means naughty
L is the abbreviation for line, so two of them make LL

explanation.surface: Just two lines of a racy verse.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballad is a narrative poem or song, often in short stanzas.

clue.text: Gigantic bird's limited movement from side to side

indicators.note: limited means the word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: to rock is to sway from side to side

explanation.surface: A huge bird that can barely sway.
explanation.definitionFit: The roc is an enormous mythical bird from Arabian legend.

clue.text: Mad cry of one favouring the democratic vote, say?

definitions.text: cry of one favouring the democratic vote, say?
definitions.meaning: a cheer of support for the ballot, sounding like 'up the poll'

explanation.surface: A voting enthusiast's slogan doubles as a word for being crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading puns on POLE and POLL, a vote, flagged by 'say?'.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang uses this idiom for being mad or crazy.

clue.text: It's pale yellow and loose in Slough

indicators.note: in puts the word for loose inside the word for marsh

parts.note: a slough is a bog, and a fen is marshland
lax means loose or slack

explanation.surface: A colour description that sounds like something in a Berkshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: Slough is also a town west of London; here it means a bog.
explanation.definitionFit: Flaxen describes the pale yellow colour of flax fibre, often of hair.

clue.text: Speed with which vehicle's gutted before gangster leaves district

indicators.note: before puts the first piece ahead of the second
gutted means the insides are removed, keeping only the outer letters
leaves means the gangster's name departs from the word for district

parts.note: a locality is a district
Al Capone was a famous gangster

explanation.surface: A getaway at pace as a crook quits the area.
explanation.definitionFit: Velocity is the rate of motion, a technical word for speed.

clue.text: Spinner found among craggy rocks

indicators.note: found among says the answer sits within the letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Something spinning discovered amid rugged boulders.
explanation.definitionFit: A gyro, short for gyroscope, is a spinning wheel that keeps its orientation.

clue.text: Equality sought at first in part of Oxon plant

indicators.note: in puts equality and an initial letter inside the place name

parts.note: Cowley is a district of Oxford, in Oxfordshire (Oxon)
par means equality, as in on a par

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of sought

explanation.surface: A campaign for equal rights in an Oxfordshire suburb.
explanation.definitionFit: Cow parsley is a common hedgerow plant with white umbrella-shaped flowerheads.

clue.text: Novel stool ultimately needing varnishing

parts.note: She is a novel by H. Rider Haggard

indicators.note: ultimately takes the last letter of stool

parts.note: lacking means needing or wanting

explanation.surface: Fiction about a stool that wants a coat of varnish.
explanation.definitionFit: Shellac is a resin varnish, so applying it is varnishing.

clue.text: Reportedly check out whatever area for lengths of time

indicators.note: reportedly says the words are spoken, giving a sound to be spelled differently

parts.note: check out means try, and whatever means any

explanation.surface: A survey of any region said to take a long while.
explanation.definitionFit: Triennia is the plural of triennium, a period of three years.

clue.text: Thuggish players may use it to get supporters plastered

parts.note: rough means violent or thuggish
the cast is the set of actors in a play

explanation.surface: A brutal acting troupe getting their fans drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: Supporters here are walls and pillars, and plastered means coated, not drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Roughcast is a coarse plaster of lime and gravel used on outside walls.

clue.text: Flirted endlessly going over this island

indicators.note: going over means the shortened word is turned back to front
endlessly means the final letter is removed

parts.note: toyed means flirted or trifled

explanation.surface: Dallying endlessly on a trip over to an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts TOYED to TOYE; 'going over' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyot is a small island in a river, also spelt ait.

clue.text: One often gets depressed, producing no letters

definitions.text: One often gets depressed, producing no letters

parts.words: One often gets depressed, producing no letters
parts.note: a keyboard key that is pressed down constantly but prints only a gap

explanation.definitionFit: The space bar is the long keyboard key that types a blank between words.

clue.text: I bother no end about Islamic ascetic

indicators.note: about turns the whole of the preceding pair backwards
no end means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: fuss means bother

explanation.surface: Endlessly troubling a Muslim holy man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no end' cuts FUSS to FUS; 'about' reverses I+FUS.
explanation.definitionFit: A Sufi is a Muslim mystic following an ascetic path.

clue.text: The writer's senior, retaining power to reclaim land

parts.note: the writer is the setter, so the writer's means I'm (I am)
older means senior

explanation.surface: An elderly author who keeps hold of the energy needed to recover ground.
explanation.definitionFit: To impolder is to reclaim land from the sea, making a Dutch-style polder.

clue.text: Old city man demanding speedy action

parts.note: Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia
a gent is a man

explanation.surface: A man from an ancient city who wants things done fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Urgent describes something pressing that requires immediate attention.

clue.text: Tart involved with choice of priestly government

indicators.note: involved suggests the letters are tangled together into a new order

explanation.surface: A pastry mixed up with the selection of clerical rulers.
explanation.definitionFit: Theocratic describes rule by priests or a religious authority.

clue.text: Complain, pay-and-display area being out of the ark!

indicators.note: being out of means the boat's letters are removed from the parking word

parts.note: a car park often has pay-and-display ticket machines
the ark is Noah's boat

explanation.surface: Grumbling about a parking lot that seems ancient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of the ark' is an idiom for very old-fashioned.
explanation.definitionFit: To carp is to find fault or grumble pettily.

clue.text: Elgar's variation for portable organ

indicators.note: variation suggests the composer's name is rearranged, echoing his Enigma Variations

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A piece by Elgar arranged for a small keyboard instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A regal is a small portable reed organ of the Renaissance.

clue.text: Daughter's always getting time off, it dawns on us

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter
ay (or aye) is an old word for always
a break is time off

explanation.surface: A daughter perpetually given holidays.
explanation.definitionFit: Daybreak is dawn, the moment the day begins.

clue.text: Possibly nurse's buzzer

parts.note: a hospital call button is the decoy; a nurse in a hive is a worker that tends larvae and buzzes

explanation.definitionFit: Nurse bees are young workers in a hive that feed the larvae.

clue.text: Possibly Bailey's game?

definitions.meaning: a Bailey is a prefabricated military crossing made of steel panels
a card game for four players

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a pastime belongs to someone named Bailey.
explanation.definitionFit: A Bailey bridge is a portable crossing; the card game is played in pairs.

clue.text: Vouch for retired volunteers guarding badger's burrow

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the whole combination is read backwards
guarding means the volunteers surround the burrow

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve
a sett is a badger's den

explanation.surface: Ex-reservists protecting a badger's home will speak up for it.
explanation.definitionFit: To attest is to bear witness or certify that something is true.

clue.text: Wander round goods left in untidy state

indicators.note: round means the word for wander goes around the other letters

parts.note: to stray is to wander
G is the abbreviation for good, so two make GG

explanation.surface: A drifter circling merchandise, leaving it in a mess.
explanation.definitionFit: Straggly means growing or spreading untidily.
